summary: A compact east-of-Ping neighbourhood food wander, with a useful anchor at Kanomjeen Sanpakoi in Talat Thong Kham and plenty of nearby everyday cafés and noodle shops. This is a set of operating businesses, not one single attraction; hours and stalls vary.
whyGo: Try khanom jeen nam ngiao, a northern tomato-and-pork noodle curry, at a long-running market stall, then browse the surrounding food market.
The broader San Pa Khoi/Charoen Mueang quarter has coffee, noodles and northern Thai dinner options within a walkable area.
bestFor: Independent food explorers who enjoy informal markets and can navigate menus or point to dishes.
A flexible half-day/evening that pairs with the railway station or the Wat Ket riverside quarter.
skipIf: You need a fully predictable itinerary, extensive English menus, or guaranteed dietary separation.
You cannot manage uneven pavements, crowded market aisles or low seating without assistance.
duration: Plan 1.5–3 hours for a focused market meal and nearby walk; allow longer if adding cafés or dinner. These are planning estimates.
cost: Budget about ฿100–300 per person for a simple noodle meal, snacks and a drink; estimate only. A recent Wongnai review reports noodle portions below ฿100, but prices can change.
hours: Kanomjeen Sanpakoi is currently listed 11:00–23:00, with a recent listing/reviews indicating Sunday closure. San Pa Khoi Market is described as an early-morning market; individual market vendors have different hours. Recheck locally before setting out.
bestTime: Go early morning for the fresh market atmosphere, or arrive around lunch/early dinner for the khanom jeen stall. December is generally more comfortable for walking than the hot season, but crowds and exact vendor schedules vary.
gettingThere: From the Old City, cross the Ping eastward by taxi/Grab or songthaew; the neighbourhood is a short ride away. A current neighbourhood guide estimates under ten minutes from the Old City and about ten minutes from Nimman by car, traffic dependent. Aim for Talat Thong Kham / Kanomjeen Sanpakoi, 11/1 Soi Tha Satoi, then walk between nearby stops. The wider quarter is walkable; allow for uneven pavements.
booking: No booking needed for the market and casual noodle stalls. Go early or outside peak meal times to reduce queues. Check live listings or call ahead if travelling specifically for one stall.
accessibility: Market paths and footways may be crowded, narrow or uneven; seating is informal and toilets/access arrangements are not reliably documented. Step-free access and accessible facilities are unverified. A car drop-off near the chosen restaurant can reduce walking.
practicalTips: Order at the counter and pay first at the khanom jeen stall; recent customer guidance says to find a table, then clear dishes after eating.
Nam ngiao is a pork-based northern curry; the stall also lists several curry sauces and chicken khao soi. Ask in Thai about ingredients and cross-contact.
Vegetarian, vegan, halal and allergy-safe preparation are not confirmed. Fish sauce, shrimp paste, meat stock and shared utensils are common risks; do not assume a dish is suitable.
Carry small cash and save the Thai name ขนมจีนสันป่าข่อย / ตลาดทองคำ to show a driver.
decemberNotes: December 2026 operating schedules and any special market events have not been published in the sources checked. Treat the regular hours as a guide only; verify close to the visit, especially around public holidays. The area is also described as an early-morning fresh market, so do not assume every food stall runs all day.
uncertainties: Hours and prices are drawn from current third-party listings and recent user reviews rather than a venue-owned page; they may change before December 2026.
Accessibility details, payment methods, exact transport fares and dietary cross-contact practices are not published reliably.
The photo is a user-contributed image of a khanom jeen stall associated with San Pa Khoi Market, not a guaranteed current view of the stall. Reuse permission is not established.
